data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The test should assert a property of the admission process itself\u2014specifically, that the process only commits artifacts that are well-evidenced\u2014rather than asserting a static property of the resulting artifact set.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the admission process's internal logic is opaque or not exposed for testing, this assertion cannot be verified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the process admits well-evidenced artifacts but fails to store them correctly, this test passes while the system is broken at the storage layer.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Directly embodying SRC_005's central thesis, the test checks the process's admission criteria (e.g., evidence threshold met) for each commit, not the count. This aligns with the unifier (SRC_003) by seeking the covering principle at the process level and with the empiric (SRC_004) by grounding the test in observable process behavior. Published testing principles supporting this include 'Test Behavior, Not Implementation' and 'Test Invariants, Not States' when states are volatile.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
